channel.description: Latest articles from The GW Hatchet (gwhatchet.com)

item.title: Late-game collapse sinks men’s basketball in 89-75 loss to VCU
item.description: Men's basketball's second half woes continued in 89-75 loss to Virginia Commonwealth on Tuesday.

item.title: Perspective: I voted for Trump in 2024. Then I marched against ICE in Minneapolis
item.description: When I cast my vote for President Donald Trump in the 2024 election, I was pledging my loyalty to the American people — not to the Republican Party. I also flew to Minneapolis to partake in the protests against ICE.

item.title: Dish of the Week: DC Tasty Corner’s Argentine beef empanadas
item.description: A bright red building off Wisconsin Avenue in Georgetown blends South American flair with American comfort, dishing out everything from flaky empanadas to hearty falafel bowls, a menu built to satisfy virtually any craving.

item.title: Women’s basketball upsets top A-10 contender Richmond 57-54 in overtime
item.description: Women’s basketball snuck past Richmond 57-54 in an overtime thriller in the Smith CenterWednesday night.

item.title: New GW Law public interest dean focused on student professional, funding opportunities
item.description: GW Law officials named Matt Nosanchuk as its next as its next Lerner family associate dean of public interest and public service law following the retirement of former Associate Dean Alan Morrison after 16 years at the helm.

item.title: Bowser declares Potomac sewage spill a public emergency
item.description: Bowser's order comes as over 250 million gallons of wastewater has spilled into the Potomac River, heightening bacteria levels.

item.title: Officials unveil open access policy years after Faculty Senate resolution
item.description: The adoption of the policy follows advocacy from faculty after the Faculty Senate narrowly passed a resolution in 2015 supporting an open access policy.

item.title: Rwandan ambassador talks country’s diaspora, post-genocide recovery
item.description: Rwanda’s ambassador to the United States said reconciliation efforts, diaspora engagement and constitutional reforms expanding women’s political representation laid the foundation for the country’s recovery after its 1994 genocide.

item.title: South Block to open Western Market location in March
item.description: South Block, a Foggy Bottom-based smoothie chain, will open its second location in the Foggy Bottom neighborhood in March.
